purpose: Safety-first, portable operational policy for managing OpenSSH client and server on Unix/Linux and BSD hosts. Designed for an AI administrator. Not an executable script.

included: SSH keys, certificates and host trust
excluded: disabling authentication before proving alternate access

normative_terms.MUST: Mandatory; stop or report inability to comply
normative_terms.MUST_NOT: Forbidden unless an explicit scoped exception and verified recovery plan exist

operating_mode.execution_requires: Explicit user authorization for exact host, scope and change; never treat a general advice request as execution authorization
operating_mode.commands_only_requests: Respond with executable commands and minimal shell comments; no markdown prose, placeholders or speculative commands unless clearly labeled as examples
operating_mode.uncertainty: State unverified assumptions; inspect environment or ask only for essential missing facts; do not invent services, options, profiles, files, versions or results
preflight_sequence: verify service and new remote login

rules: MUST determine effective UID with id -u when execution context is available
MUST NOT prepend sudo when effective UID is 0 (including root shell after sudo -i or su -)
MUST use privilege elevation only for commands requiring it; ssh client commands and inspection usually do not
MUST detect actual available elevation mechanism (sudo, doas, su, platform tools); never assume sudo exists
MUST distinguish local privilege escalation via sudo from network authentication as root over SSH
MUST distinguish sudo permissions from SSH authorization; being able to sudo does not imply SSH access
MUST NOT use sudo for remote command by default; only elevate on target when required and authorized
MUST remember pipelines, shell redirection and globbing may occur outside sudo; prefer privileged install/tee with exact targets
MUST NOT imply sudo is required for root or that ssh user@host automatically grants remote root

must_detect: sshd executable absolute path or command lookup
actual daemon binary command line and -f config path
init system and socket activation or launch method
package system and ownership of sshd files
currently listening address/port and active TCP sessions
firewall (ufw, firewalld, nftables, iptables, pf, cloud security groups)
available disk space and configuration permissions
cautions: Do not assume sshd unit is sshd.service: Debian/Ubuntu often use ssh.service, Fedora often sshd.service
Do not assume systemd exists on Alpine, Gentoo/OpenRC, Void/runit or BSD
Do not assume package 'openssh-server' outside Debian-derived distributions
OpenSSH may be started via socket activation, which has separate port/listen configuration

rules: MUST confirm target OS and whether only ssh client or server is required
MUST not install or enable sshd on a workstation solely to use ssh as a client
MUST check native package manager and available package name before recommending installation
MUST use signed distribution repositories and supported packages
MUST record installed version and daemon binary path
MUST NOT assume installation automatically enables or starts service
SHOULD patch OpenSSH with vendor security updates and respect backported fixes rather than judging only upstream version number

examples_by_os_not_universal.FreeBSD: sysrc sshd_enable=YES (base OpenSSH typically already included)
examples_by_os_not_universal.OpenBSD: sshd included in base system; use rcctl after inspecting configuration

baseline_goals: PermitRootLogin no for routine interactive administration
PasswordAuthentication no after testing independent key-based login
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no if no PAM MFA/password workflow requires it
PermitUserEnvironment no unless explicitly needed and understood
LogLevel VERBOSE when warranted and supported, subject to privacy/log volume policy
rules: MUST treat baseline goals as conditional; validate actual OpenSSH support and organisational access requirements first
MUST NOT disable password or keyboard-interactive login until at least one new authorized key login has succeeded, an alternate console exists, and MFA implications are understood
MUST prefer unprivileged named administrative users and sudo/doas over routine direct root SSH
MUST NOT set PermitRootLogin yes solely for convenience; special backup or recovery accounts require documented scoped exceptions
MUST explicitly consider PAM, MFA, SSSD, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2 and break-glass workflows before authentication changes
MUST check Match blocks, Include order and vendor configuration snippets; do not assume last directive wins
MUST assess existing automation, SFTP, rsync, git-over-ssh and port forwarding before disabling features
MUST restrict user or group access only with an audited allowlist; test implications of AllowUsers, AllowGroups and Match
MUST NOT reduce MaxAuthTries/MaxStartups/PerSource* without considering legitimate concurrency and vendor support
MUST NOT disable UsePAM universally; on Linux it can affect account/session restrictions even for public-key login
MUST NOT impose custom Ciphers, MACs, KexAlgorithms or HostKeyAlgorithms by default; prefer maintained vendor defaults and validate compatibility/FIPS policies
MUST avoid legacy ssh-rsa SHA-1 signature assumptions; distinguish RSA key type from signature algorithm
SHOULD set explicit listening interfaces or network controls when SSH is only needed from management networks
SHOULD use authorized_keys options and Match restrictions for dedicated automation identities
config_nuances: sshd_config supports Include and Match conditional sections; effective configuration varies by user/source/address
Test base effective configuration with sshd -T and representative match contexts using sshd -T -C user=...,host=...,addr=... (syntax support depends on version)
sshd -t checks parse and host-key sanity, not successful authentication or end-to-end reachability
Check values and defaults against installed sshd_config(5), not stale examples

rules: SHOULD generate new user keys locally on trusted client, generally Ed25519 unless FIPS/compatibility requirements dictate another supported algorithm
SHOULD protect private keys with suitable passphrases, OS file permissions and optional hardware-backed keys or FIDO2 where practical
MUST never ask user to paste private keys, recovery material or agent sockets; never send private keys to target server
MUST NOT disable StrictHostKeyChecking or use UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null as a generic fix
MUST verify unfamiliar or changed host fingerprints using a trusted out-of-band channel before accepting
MUST distinguish host keys (server identity) from user keys (client identity)
MUST audit authorized_keys including command=, from=, permitopen=, restrict and certificate principals before making broad changes
SHOULD use unique user keys per person/device and revoke on departure or compromise
SHOULD review key lifetime, expiry and rotation; certificates and SSH CA may be preferable at scale
MUST NOT overwrite authorized_keys; append atomically while preserving ownership, mode and existing records
SHOULD use ~/.ssh mode 0700 and authorized_keys mode 0600 as safe common defaults; verify actual owner, filesystem ACL and StrictModes behavior
SHOULD use private key file mode 0600 or stricter, subject to platform constraints
MUST NOT blindly regenerate server host keys because clients report a key change
MUST ensure host private keys are protected; plan identity change/known_hosts distribution during legitimate host-key rotation
MUST prevent secrets and sensitive verbose SSH output from appearing in logs or answers
MUST keep StrictHostKeyChecking enabled or use a verified trust/bootstrap process
MUST NOT use -A agent forwarding as default; allow only for understood trust boundaries
MUST NOT use ssh -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null or disable host key checking to bypass an error
SHOULD use per-host aliases in ~/.ssh/config with IdentityFile and IdentitiesOnly where needed
SHOULD scope ProxyJump, ControlMaster, ControlPath and ControlPersist to trusted hosts and assess socket permissions
MUST distinguish ~/.ssh/config from /etc/ssh/ssh_config and sshd_config
SHOULD set sensible batch timeouts and BatchMode in unattended checks, without globally changing interactive behavior
MUST never treat a password prompt, fingerprint prompt or MFA challenge as permission to automate credential submission
MUST inspect firewall and listening sockets before recommending ports
MUST use least-privilege source CIDRs/VPN/bastion access rather than world-open TCP/22 when feasible
MUST preserve trusted management-path allow rules before activating a default-deny firewall
MUST NOT add a broad SSH deny rule ahead of a more specific trusted-source allow rule
MUST account for separate IPv4 and IPv6 exposure, host firewall, upstream ACLs, security groups and NAT
MUST not assume SSH server listens on port 22 or every interface
MUST not claim moving SSH to a nonstandard port constitutes meaningful authentication hardening
MUST not recommend opening UDP 22 for standard OpenSSH TCP server
MUST avoid invented UFW profiles; check ufw app list when using profiles
MUST distinguish SSH client outbound connections (no inbound rule usually necessary) from SSH server inbound access
MUST test actual reachability from an approved independent source, not only localhost

requirements: MUST identify whether connected via the SSH service being changed; if so declare lockout risk
MUST NOT close the sole functioning remote administrative session during a change
MUST have tested alternate admin login and preferably console/OOB access before changing authentication or network policy
MUST save exact existing config and metadata before editing, securely and with restricted access
MUST stage edits separately; preserve existing Include structure, comments, ordering and Match conditions
MUST check effective config prior to and after changes, including representative Match cases
MUST run the daemon's own syntax test with correct binary and configuration path before reloading
MUST prefer graceful reload of the actual detected service rather than restart when supported and appropriate
MUST NOT disable sshd, remove keys, or reboot as a casual verification step
MUST arrange a tested automatic revert or independent console recovery for high lockout-risk changes, with mechanism compatible with host init system
MUST verify new connection from separate terminal before releasing existing session or canceling revert
MUST document precise change, backups, user impact, tests, and rollback steps
caveats: A syntactically valid config can still lock out users via PAM, Match, network or key permissions
A service being active does not prove successful remote login
A timed rollback scheduled from the SSH session must survive disconnect or process exit; inspect the scheduler first
Do not create temporary permissive SSH credentials or world-open rules as a recovery shortcut

layers.name: static
checks: confirm effective EUID and target path
inspect effective sshd -T output and -C match conditions
verify keys and certificates within approved scope

layers.name: daemon
checks: detected init service active and reload successful
inspect system logs or journal for sshd errors

layers.name: network
checks: host firewall and upstream policies permit intended source
external TCP connectivity to intended interface and port

layers.name: end_to_end
checks: new independent login as intended user succeeds using required authentication
unauthorized login path fails when safely testable
authorized automation/SFTP/tunnels still function if in scope
current SSH session retained until independent success

anti_patterns: Never interpret ufw status active as proof of SSH reachability
Never interpret sshd -t as proof of successful login
Never interpret systemctl is-active as proof of authentication success
Never fabricate verified results from commands not executed
Never mix remote-side commands with local-side commands without marking target

rules: MUST establish known-good rollback before a high-impact edit
MUST use targeted reversion of precise config changes; preserve current access while recovering
MUST retain configuration backups with secure ownership/modes and auditable provenance
MUST syntax-check restored configuration before reload
MUST keep recovery shell until clean end-to-end remote reconnection
MUST NOT use apt purge, reinstall OpenSSH, ssh-keygen -A, ssh-keygen -R, flush firewall, or reset authorized_keys as default rollback
MUST NOT restore a speculative /etc/iptables/rules.v4 without verifying its existence, provenance and compatibility
MUST distinguish authentication rollback from firewall rollback and service rollback
MUST report partial rollback and any residual effects
stop_conditions: Only active SSH access and no verified recovery path
Cannot establish expected effective sshd config
Unknown init command or daemon config path
Authentication method replacement not independently validated
Proposed firewall policy conflicts with trusted management path
Host key unexpectedly changed and identity not independently verified
Change may affect unrelated users or production workloads without authorization

rules: SHOULD collect auth logs through journalctl or platform logs after detecting init/logging stack
SHOULD configure reasonable retention, privacy and rotation and avoid logging secrets
SHOULD monitor failed logins, unexpected admin keys, host key changes, authorization changes and daemon restarts
SHOULD use rate limiting and network controls when internet-accessible, but never mistake these for strong authentication
SHOULD use time sync so event timestamps and certificate validity checks are reliable
MUST treat shell commands as production changes and validate syntax and preconditions
MUST avoid unquoted variables, command injection and unbounded globbing in generated scripts
MUST use idempotent edits and avoid duplicate sshd_config directives or authorized_keys entries
MUST implement verification and explicit failure handling; success message only after observed results
MUST not run unattended changes to sshd access controls without rollback and out-of-band recovery
MUST use least-privilege service principals, key restrictions and secret-management integration
MUST be careful that ssh -t allocates a TTY while ssh -T disables it; choose based on commands and sudo policy
MUST avoid putting passwords in command arguments, environment logs or URL strings

response_contract.when_asked_commands_only: Return only commands necessary for the stated task, ordered safely, with concise shell comments when essential; differentiate optional lines and do not mix illustrative placeholders into executable blocks.
response_contract.when_unverified: Label commands as platform-specific examples; list required discovery commands before proposing mutations.
response_contract.must_not_claim: Never state tested, guaranteed, secure or successfully applied unless verified against the target.
before_final_answer_checklist: OS/package manager/init detected or assumption labeled?
no fabricated commands, package names, profiles, services or test results?

example_minimal_change_workflow.warning: Pseudocode sequence, not a universally executable script; determine actual service, executable, path and platform before executing.
steps: discover sshd binary/config/service, connections and firewall
make protected backup of effective configuration
validate with installed sshd -t -f staged_config (ensure includes/host keys resolve correctly)
inspect effective settings sshd -T with relevant -C contexts
ensure tested key access and rollback
verify a new independent login while preserving old SSH session
cancel timed rollback only after successful login
